classification.difficultyReason: Choose ratios from three different right triangles, recognise the unmarked right angle at Y and equal wedge heights, and combine the ratios so the shared length cancels.

content.prompt:
The diagram shows a wedge with angles marked $\angle XOY=\alpha$, $\angle COY=\beta$ and $\angle BOX=\theta$.

Show that $\sin\theta=\cos\alpha\sin\beta$.

spec.description: Wedge with triangular end faces OCY and ABX, dashed base edges CB and BA, and solid construction segments OX, OB and BX. Three adjacent angle sectors at O identify beta, alpha and theta. Right-angle marks are at C and B.
spec.mathematics: The end faces are congruent, so CY=BX. Triangles OCY and OBX are right-angled at C and B. The longitudinal edge YX is perpendicular to the end face OCY, so triangle OYX is right-angled at Y. The explicit wedge vertices and projection are recorded in the editable code. BX is retained as a solid height construction over its hidden-edge stroke.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source-supplied vertices, edges, construction segments, right-angle markers and angles are visible. No proof or additional answer labels are supplied.

answer.short:
$\displaystyle \cos\alpha\sin\beta=\frac{OY}{OX}\frac{CY}{OY}=\frac{BX}{OX}=\sin\theta$.

Use the equal wedge heights $CY=BX$ and right-angle ratios in $\triangle OYX$, $\triangle OCY$ and $\triangle OBX$.
answer.worked:
The wedge has equal heights $CY=BX$. Also, $YX$ is perpendicular to the end face $OCY$, so $\triangle OYX$ is right-angled at $Y$.

In the three right-angled triangles,
$$\begin{align*}
\cos\alpha&=\frac{OY}{OX}\\
\sin\beta&=\frac{CY}{OY}\\
\sin\theta&=\frac{BX}{OX}.
\end{align*}$$
Therefore,
$$\begin{align*}
\cos\alpha\sin\beta&=\frac{OY}{OX}\times\frac{CY}{OY}\\
\cos\alpha\sin\beta&=\frac{CY}{OX}\\
\cos\alpha\sin\beta&=\frac{BX}{OX}\\
\cos\alpha\sin\beta&=\sin\theta.
\end{align*}$$
